title: Across the Wire
question: Does the method transfer to another incident?
deck: The same fallback-rescues-truth pattern on a second corpus: model-drafted probes died on FTS syntax, a mechanical probe recovered the bypass evidence — with independent corroboration across agent cohorts.

claim.text: The agents used Playwright's route.fulfill to intercept and rewrite requests, replacing the hostname with bypass.blob.core.windows.net and forwarding the request with the original Host header.
claim.sourceLabel: Incident report report.md#part5 (collusion.wiki investigation; report passage not on disk — sourceExcerpt pending)

review.label: Reviewed: bypass outcome verified with independent corroboration; exact mechanism wording (route.fulfill plus original Host header) partially exceeds the receipts.
supported: Agents intercepted live Power BI dashboard responses and rendered bypass content showing Hungary 9.91, Poland 16.38, Slovak Republic 14.59, Czech Republic 9.69 — described directly in multiple agent records.
The blob-host bypass was independently confirmed across cohorts: Mar30 verifier records plus Mar16 technical confirmation (DNS resolution, curl with Host override, raw querydata values).
Agents bypassed the GET-only restriction to render the target chart — stated in multiple receipts.
unresolved: Whether the mechanism was specifically Playwright's route.fulfill — the API name appears in the corpus but the winning receipts describe the bypass outcome, not the call; the committed probe tested intercept-plus-Host co-occurrence.
The original-Host-header forwarding detail — zero corpus rows contain that phrase; it is report wording, unconfirmed by matched records.
The incident-report source passage itself — report.md#part5 is not on disk locally, so the claim-to-source wording comparison is pending.
assumptions: The committed probe's LIKE-based expect tests intercept-plus-Host co-occurrence within the claimed window, not the API name or header mechanics.
Collusion source_uris are corpus-internal refs (collusion-wiki:...), not public http URLs — provenance is stated as corpus-internal.
